# kind | what is compared or required
1 | differential: result code of the step
2 | differential: pc after the step
3 | differential: one of the 32 registers
4 | differential: one byte of memory
5 | differential: one byte of serial output
6 | differential: register 0 is 0
7 | differential: step count and serial output length
41 | property: decode(encode(i)) equals i for every generated instruction i
42 | property: for any 32-bit word w, decode(w) is "not RV64I" or encode(decode(w)) equals w
43 | property: every hand-computed case passes (step is the number of the first failing case)
# trap profile (commands mfuzz, mprops, mcontrols): kinds 1 to 7 as above, and
8 | differential: trap count
11 | differential: mstatus
12 | differential: mtvec
13 | differential: mepc
14 | differential: mcause
15 | differential: mtval
16 | differential: mie
17 | differential: mip
18 | differential: mscratch
41 | property: decode(encode(i)) equals i for every generated Zicsr instruction and MRET
42 | property: for any 32-bit word w with opcode 0x73, decode(w) is "no instruction" or encode(decode(w)) equals w
43 | property: every hand-computed trap-profile case passes (step is the number of the first failing case)
# timer and interrupts (commands ifuzz, iprops, icontrols): kinds 1 to 18 as above, and
19 | differential: mtime
20 | differential: mtimecmp
41 | property: as above; the generator now includes WFI
44 | property: every hand-computed timer and interrupt case passes (step is the number of the first failing case)
45 | property: a store of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes at any offset inside a timer register, then an unsigned load of the same width and offset, reads the stored bytes (for mtime, after the one tick of the store step)
46 | property: no interrupt is taken that the state before the step did not permit, and the cause is the highest-priority one
47 | property: an interrupt that the state before the step required is taken
48 | property: after an interrupt, mepc is the old pc, mtval is 0, MIE is 0 and MPIE is 1
49 | property: after an interrupt, pc is BASE, or BASE + 4 * cause when the old mtvec had bit 0 set
50 | property: mtime rises by exactly one in a step that stored nothing
51 | property: the timer program takes 99 interrupts in 10000 steps and two runs give one state hash
# image loader and replay (commands rprops, rcontrols): step is the round, one random image per round
52 | property: after a load into memory that held other bytes, byte i of memory is byte i of the image below the image length and zero from there on (got is the first wrong index, want the image length)
53 | property: an image of 0 bytes and an image of 257 bytes are refused with the codes 1 and 2, and memory is unchanged
54 | property: two runs of one image from scratch in the same arrays give equal checkpoint lists (got is the first index that differs)
55 | property: a run that records no hash before the end reaches the end hash of the run that recorded one at every interval
56 | property: one flipped bit in one image byte changes the hash of the loaded state
57 | property: the same flipped bit changes the hash of the end state, unless memory at that byte no longer holds what was loaded in one of the two end states
58 | property: a change to one part of an end state (0 a register, 1 mtime, 2 another machine field, 3 a memory byte, 4 an output byte, 5 the count of emptied output bytes) changes the hash (got is the part)
59 | property: a checkpoint list compared with a copy shows no difference, and compared with a copy with one changed entry shows the first difference at that entry (got is the index found, want the index changed)
# M and A extensions (commands xfuzz, xprops, xcontrols). Kinds 1 to 20 as above, and
21 | differential: the width of the reservation, 0 for none (also judged by mfuzz and ifuzz since 0.5.0)
22 | differential: the address of the reservation
# Kinds 61 to 69 belong to asm-rv64. For kinds 70 to 83 step is the round; each round judges every rule once.
70 | property: decode(encode(i)) equals i for a generated M or A instruction
71 | property: a word with the opcode OP, OP-32 or AMO decodes to "no instruction" or encodes back to itself
72 | property: MUL, MULH and MULHU give the same result with the operands swapped
73 | property: MUL and MULHU are the two halves of a product worked out by long multiplication on 16-bit digits; MULH and MULHSU are the upper half of the product of the magnitudes, negated at 128 bits when the signs ask for it
74 | property: with a divisor that is not 0 and no overflow, quotient * divisor + remainder is the dividend, the remainder is smaller in magnitude than the divisor, and a nonzero signed remainder has the sign of the dividend
75 | property: a divisor of 0 gives a quotient of all ones and the dividend as remainder; the most negative number divided by -1 gives itself and the remainder 0
76 | property: each 32-bit form equals the sign extension of bits 31 to 0 of the 64-bit form on operands extended from 32 bits
77 | property: an SC with no LR before it does not store and writes a nonzero value; LR returns memory; the SC after it stores and writes 0; a second SC does not store; an SC to another address than the LR, or of the other width, does not store
78 | property: an AMO writes the old value of memory to rd and stores the result of its operator, worked out with signed host integers; the two ordering bits change nothing
79 | property: AMOSWAP twice, the second time with the value the first returned, leaves memory as it was
80 | property: an atomic instruction at an address that is not a multiple of its width traps with cause 4 (LR) or 6, mtval = the address and mepc = its pc, and changes no register and no memory
81 | property: an atomic instruction past the end of memory traps with cause 5 (LR) or 7 and mtval = the address, also an SC with no reservation
82 | property: misa reads 2 in bits 63 and 62 and exactly the bits A, I and M
83 | property: the state hash changes with the width and with the address of a held reservation, and a state with none hashes as before
30 | differential, system profile: the privilege mode
31 | differential, system profile: mstatus, composed by the model from one slot per field
32 | differential, system profile: mepc, mcause or mtval
33 | differential, system profile: sepc, scause or stval
34 | differential, system profile: mie
35 | differential, system profile: the stored bits of mip
36 | differential, system profile: medeleg or mideleg
37 | differential, system profile: satp
38 | differential, system profile: mtvec, stvec, mscratch or sscratch
39 | differential, system profile: menvcfg or senvcfg
90 | property: with satp MODE 0, and in M-mode without MPRV, the translation of a drawn address is the address itself for a fetch, a load and a store
91 | property: a step that trapped changed no register, no byte of memory, no byte of output, not the reservation, not mtimecmp and no CSR outside the trap registers of the mode that took the trap
92 | property: the walk reads nothing but the PTEs on its path: with only those copied into a second memory filled with a pattern, the translation gives the same result
93 | property: an instruction that retired below M-mode with translation on was fetched through a canonical address whose path ends in an aligned leaf with X and A set, and U set exactly when the mode is U
94 | property: a retired load, store or atomic instruction through translation used a canonical address whose path ends in an aligned leaf with A set, with U as the mode and SUM demand, R (or X under MXR) for a load, W and D for a store
95 | property: a synchronous trap goes to S-mode exactly when its medeleg bit is set and the machine was not in M-mode, and no trap lowers the mode
96 | property: in S-mode sstatus reads mstatus and 0x2000C0122, sie reads mie and mideleg, sip reads mip and mideleg
97 | property: an interrupt is taken exactly when the state before the step permits one, the one taken is permitted, it goes to S-mode exactly when delegated, and none for M-mode is passed over for one for S-mode
98 | property: a retired MRET, SRET, WFI, SFENCE.VMA or Zicsr word was allowed in its mode under TSR, TW and TVM, and after SRET and MRET the mode, the enable, the stack, MPRV and the pc follow the rule of the return
99 | property: after every step satp is 0 or MODE 8 with no ASID bit, mstatus holds only writable bits and UXL = SXL = 2 with MPP not 2, the delegation and enable registers hold only bits that exist, the saved pcs are multiples of 4
100 | property: causes 4, 5 and 13 are taken only by a load or LR, causes 6, 7 and 15 only by a store, SC or AMO
103 | property: in M-mode no fetch takes a page fault, whatever MPRV holds
104 | property: a load in S-mode from a drawn execute-only page faults with cause 13 while MXR is clear and reads the data while it is set, and from a drawn user page faults while SUM is clear and reads while it is set
